title: Signature Safe Ground
body:
The Signature Safe Ground is Manon's original design for choosing where a secondhand exchange happens, and its rule is that the ground is chosen before the price is discussed, because a place agreed under price pressure is not a choice. The design scores a proposed meeting on five qualities: public, staffed, well lit, busy at the meeting time, and easy to leave. A ground holding all five is safe ground; a ground holding three or four is daylight ground with someone told; a ground holding fewer is not ground at all, and the design's answer is a safe alternative or no deal. The insistence on a worse place after a safe alternative was offered is itself recorded as information.

Method. The working method for this record is safe-ground scoring in the Signature style. First, the five qualities are stated. Second, each quality is marked present or absent for the proposed meeting. Third, the verdict is read from the count. Fourth, the meeting place and time are told to someone, and a charged phone is carried. Fifth, the demo scores an example meeting place holding three qualities and prints the daylight-with-a-contact-told verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature safe ground. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: safe qualities: 3 of 5; public: yes; staffed: yes; well lit: NO; busy at meeting time: yes; easy to leave: NO; ground verdict: daylight only, tell someone Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every in-person secondhand exchange, without exception for small items, because small items still bring strangers together. Do not meet at a home address for a first transaction with a stranger, and do not let politeness override a bad location. Do not carry more cash than the agreed price, and do not let the meeting move at the last minute to a less public place. Do not use this design as a guarantee of safety, because a public place reduces risk rather than removing it. title: Signature Eyes-First Inspection
body:
The Signature Eyes-First Inspection is Manon's original design for the rule that the item is examined before money moves, and examined with the buyer's own eyes and hands rather than through the seller's description. The design's checklist covers appearance against the listing photographs, function tested on the spot, damage and wear examined, accessories counted, and identifying marks noted. A seller who rushes the inspection or demands payment before it is not protecting their time; they are preventing the buyer's only real check, and the design names that prevention as a failed step rather than as an inconvenience.

Method. The working method for this record is eyes-first scoring in the Signature style. First, the five inspection steps are stated. Second, each step is marked done or skipped. Third, the verdict is read: all steps done mean pay as agreed, one skipped means complete it before paying, and more skipped mean do not pay yet. Fourth, any difference from the listing is noted in writing before paying, because a difference accepted silently becomes the buyer's problem. Fifth, the demo scores an example inspection completing three of five steps and prints the do-not-pay-yet verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature eyes-first inspection. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: inspection steps done: 3 of 5; appearance matches listing: done; function tested: SKIPPED; damage and wear examined: done; accessories counted: SKIPPED; identifying marks noted: done; eyes-first verdict: do not pay yet Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand purchase, and use it strictly for electronics, furniture, and anything with moving parts or hidden wear. Do not pay before inspection for any reason, including a claim that another buyer is waiting, because that claim is pressure, not information. Do not accept an item whose serial marks have been removed or obscured without understanding why. Do not use this design as a professional appraisal, because buyer inspection is a check, not a valuation. title: Signature Platform Channel Rule
body:
The Signature Platform Channel Rule is Manon's original design for a payment rule with no exceptions: the money moves inside the platform, and the conversation stays inside the platform, because the platform channel carries the record, the identity trail, and the dispute route, and every outside channel surrenders all three at once. The rule is deliberately ungenerous to stories about fees, account problems, or discounts for paying directly, because those stories are the script by which protection is removed. A seller who will not use the channel is not offering a different payment method; they are offering a different deal, and the design refuses it.

Method. The working method for this record is channel-rule application in the Signature style. First, the platform's own payment channel is identified before price is discussed. Second, payment moves only through that channel. Third, any outside payment request is refused and kept in the message record. Fourth, insistence ends the deal and triggers a platform report. Fifth, the demo applies the rule to four example payment proposals and prints the verdict for each.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature platform channel rule. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: platform payment -> ACCEPT; bank transfer requested by seller -> REFUSE; gift cards requested by seller -> REFUSE and report; cash on collection with inspection -> ACCEPT with inspection and receipt; channel rule: inside the platform the record, the identity trail, and the dispute route all survive Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every marketplace purchase, as a household rule that no discount overrides, because the discount for paying outside is paid for with protection. Do not accept a story about platform fees or account problems as a reason to pay outside. Do not use this design as legal advice about any particular platform's terms, which govern that platform's transactions. Do not confuse paying inside the platform with paying safely in every respect, because inspection and seller checks still apply. title: Signature History Shape Reader
body:
The Signature History Shape Reader is Manon's original design for reading a seller's history as a shape rather than as a score, because scores can be inflated and shapes are harder to fake well. A genuine shape shows sales spread over months, feedback from different buyers, varied and specific wording, and problems handled openly. A manufactured shape shows a new account with a burst of praise, feedback from a few repeated accounts, identical wording, or silence followed by sudden pressure. The reader judges the shape, never a single sale, because a single sale can be arranged and a shape must be lived.

Method. The working method for this record is shape reading in the Signature style. First, the four shape signals are stated. Second, each signal is marked genuine or not for the seller. Third, the verdict is read: three or four genuine signals mean proceed with normal checks, fewer mean demand stronger inspection and platform payment, or walk away. Fourth, the failing signals are printed by name. Fifth, the demo reads an example seller history showing three genuine signals and prints the proceed verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature history shape reader. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: genuine shape signals: 3 of 4; sales spread over months: yes; feedback from varied buyers: yes; varied specific wording: NO; problems handled openly: yes; shape verdict: proceed with normal checks Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every marketplace seller, and use it hardest for high-value items and sellers with few sales. Do not treat a perfect shape as proof of honesty, because shapes can be manufactured, which is why inspection and platform payment still apply. Do not punish a new seller merely for being new; require the protections that make a new seller safe to try. Do not use this design to accuse any individual seller, because it judges patterns, not people. title: Signature Handover Album
body:
The Signature Handover Album is Manon's original design for fixing an item's state at the moment of transfer in photographs, because a dispute after handover is decided by what can be shown, and memory is the weakest exhibit. The album holds five shots: overall condition, close views of wear or damage, identifying marks, included accessories, and the item with its listing or agreed description. Taken before payment, the album fixes the state at transfer and protects both sides equally; taken afterward, it proves only that a photograph was taken, which is why the album's rule is timing first and completeness second.

Method. The working method for this record is album checking in the Signature style. First, the five shots are stated. Second, each shot is marked taken or missing before payment. Third, the verdict is read: all five taken mean the handover is documented, any missing mean take the missing shot before paying. Fourth, damage found in the album that the listing did not disclose triggers renegotiation or walking away before paying. Fifth, the demo checks an example album with all five shots taken and prints the documented verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature handover album. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: album shots taken: 5 of 5; overall condition: taken; wear and damage close-ups: taken; identifying marks: taken; included accessories: taken; item with listing: taken; album verdict: handover documented Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand handover, and use it strictly for high-value items, electronics, and anything where condition is the deal. Do not photograph another person's private property beyond the item being sold, and do not use photographs to embarrass or threaten the other party. Do not rely on the platform's listing photographs alone, because listings change and handover condition is what matters. Do not use this design as legal advice about evidence, which is governed by the applicable dispute route's own rules. title: Signature Device Proving Bench
body:
The Signature Device Proving Bench is Manon's original design for proving a secondhand electronic device works before it is bought, because electronics fail in ways photographs cannot show: batteries that die in minutes, screens with dead zones, ports that charge only at one angle, speakers that crackle at volume, and account locks that appear only after sign-in. The bench's test is short and agreed before meeting: power on, screen and input, sound, ports and charging, and account or activation status, all operated by the buyer's own hands. A seller who will not allow the bench is protecting the sale, not the device.

Method. The working method for this record is bench testing in the Signature style. First, the five bench tests are stated. Second, each test is run in front of the seller and marked pass or fail. Third, the verdict is read: all passed mean pay as agreed, one failed means renegotiate or walk away, and an activation lock present means do not buy until the seller removes it in front of you. Fourth, the results are recorded with the handover album. Fifth, the demo runs the bench on an example device passing all five tests and prints the pay verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature device proving bench. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: bench tests passed: 5 of 5; powers on and holds charge briefly: pass; display and input work: pass; sound clear: pass; charging and ports work: pass; no account or activation lock: pass; bench verdict: pay as agreed Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand electronic device, including phones, laptops, consoles, and audio gear. Do not buy a device still signed into the previous owner's account or locked to it, because such a device may become unusable and its history is not yours to inherit. Do not accept a test performed only by the seller's hands; the buyer operates the device. Do not use this design as a professional diagnostic, because bench testing finds common faults, not every fault. title: Signature Price Compass
body:
The Signature Price Compass is Manon's original design for pointing at the typical price before desire points at the bargain, because a price far below the range other sellers ask is information, not luck. The compass gathers comparable listings for the same item in similar condition, takes the middle value as the typical price, and measures the asking price's distance below it. A modest distance is plausible; a large distance with a disclosed reason demands harder inspection; a large distance with no reason is treated as a lure until inspection proves otherwise. Genuine reasons for a low price exist, and the compass's job is to require the reason to be shown in the item, not told in a story.

Method. The working method for this record is compass computation in the Signature style. First, three comparable prices are stated as worked-example inputs. Second, the typical price is taken as the middle value. Third, the asking price's distance below typical is computed as a percentage. Fourth, the verdict is read from the distance bands. Fifth, the demo compares an example asking price with three comparables and prints the distance and verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature price compass. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: comparable prices: [90.0, 100.0, 110.0]; typical price: 100.00; asking price: 95.00; below typical by: 5.0%; compass verdict: plausible Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand purchase where the price is the main attraction, and use it strictly for branded and high-value goods. Do not use a low price alone as proof of fraud, because genuine bargains exist and insulting a genuine seller loses a good deal. Do not use a typical price computed from too few or incomparable listings; condition, accessories, and age must match. Do not let the compass override inspection, because even a fairly priced item can be faulty. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

title: Signature Brand Pattern Check
body:
The Signature Brand Pattern Check is Manon's original design for judging a branded secondhand item by its pattern rather than by its logo, because logos are the easiest feature to copy and good fakes copy single features well. The pattern covers markings matched against the manufacturer's own information, materials and finish, serial or code plausibility, packaging and documentation consistency, and a price gap explained. No single check proves genuineness; the verdict comes from the pattern, and a pattern with several failures is a refusal even when the item looks convincing, because the pattern is the authentication and the logo is only its nickname.

Method. The working method for this record is pattern scoring in the Signature style. First, the five pattern checks are stated. Second, the item is examined against each check. Third, the verdict is read: four or five passes mean proceed with normal checks, three mean seek an expert opinion before paying, and fewer mean do not buy. Fourth, the examination photographs join the handover album. Fifth, the demo scores an example branded item passing two checks and prints the do-not-buy verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature brand pattern check. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: pattern checks passed: 2 of 5; markings match manufacturer info: FAIL; materials and finish match: pass; serial or code plausible: FAIL; packaging and documents consistent: pass; price gap explained: FAIL; pattern verdict: do not buy Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for branded goods, safety-critical goods, and any item where the brand carries the value or the safety. Do not use a convincing logo alone as proof. Do not buy safety-critical counterfeits at any price, because the failure mode is injury rather than disappointment. Do not use this design as an expert authentication, because expert authentication is a separate service with its own methods. title: Signature High-Value Ledger
body:
The Signature High-Value Ledger is Manon's original design for high-value secondhand purchases, and its principle is that the ordinary routine is necessary but not sufficient when the price justifies more fraud and the faults cost more to discover. The ledger's entries are documentary: ownership and history records checked, identifying numbers matched to documents, independent inspection completed, payment channel recorded, and a written agreement of price and condition. A seller who resists documentary checks for a high-value item is not being private; they are asking the buyer to carry a risk the documents would have carried, and the ledger refuses that transfer.

Method. The working method for this record is ledger scoring in the Signature style. First, the five ledger entries are stated. Second, each entry is marked done or missing. Third, the verdict is read: all done mean proceed, one missing means complete it before paying, and more missing mean do not pay yet. Fourth, the documents join the transaction record. Fifth, the demo scores an example high-value purchase completing three of five entries and prints the do-not-pay-yet verdict.

Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Do not skip the independent inspection for a vehicle or a complex machine, because a buyer's eye cannot see internal wear. Do not accept documents that do not match the item's identifying numbers. title: Signature Parcel Covenant
body:
The Signature Parcel Covenant is Manon's original design for the agreement that must exist before a secondhand parcel moves, because after dispatch the buyer cannot inspect and the seller cannot re-pack, and every ambiguity becomes a dispute. The covenant covers who pays shipping, which tracked service is used, how the item is packed and photographed before dispatch, what happens if the item arrives damaged, and who bears the return cost if the item is not as described. Written in the platform's messages, the covenant is evidence; left verbal or vague, it is a misunderstanding waiting for a damaged parcel to reveal it.

Method. The working method for this record is covenant checking with cost arithmetic in the Signature style. First, the five covenant points are stated. Second, each point is marked agreed or open. Third, the buyer's total is computed as item price plus the buyer's share of shipping, using stated example prices clearly labeled as worked-example inputs. Fourth, the verdict is read: all points agreed mean dispatch, any open point means agree it in writing first. Fifth, the demo checks an example covenant with all points agreed and prints the dispatch verdict with the total.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature parcel covenant. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: buyer total (example prices): 69.00; open covenant points: []; covenant verdict: dispatch Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand shipment, and use it strictly for fragile, high-value, and hard-to-replace items. Do not accept an untracked shipment for a valuable item, because untracked delivery cannot be proven. Do not accept vague packing promises; require a description of the packing and a pre-dispatch photograph. Do not use this design as a substitute for the carrier's and platform's own shipping terms, which govern the specific shipment. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

title: Signature Return Accord
body:
The Signature Return Accord is Manon's original design for the return terms of a private sale, and its premise is that private sellers sell as seen and described, so protection comes from accurate description, inspection, and the platform's rules rather than from a general right to change one's mind. The accord therefore fixes five terms before payment: the accuracy standard, the reporting deadline, the return shipping payer, the refund timing, and the evidence required. Agreed in writing, these terms are fair to both sides; assumed silently, they are a dispute, and the accord exists to prevent the silence.

Method. The working method for this record is accord checking in the Signature style. First, the five accord terms are stated. Second, each term is marked agreed or open. Third, the verdict is read: all agreed mean proceed on understood terms, any open mean agree it in writing before paying. Fourth, after delivery, a not-as-described problem is reported within the agreed deadline with photographs, because late reports lose credibility even when true. Fifth, the demo checks an example accord with one open term and prints the agree-first verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature return accord. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: accord terms agreed: 4 of 5; open terms: ['return shipping payer agreed']; accord verdict: agree the open terms in writing first Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand purchase, and use it strictly for items bought without inspection, such as shipped goods. Do not assume a right to return for change of mind in a private sale unless the seller or platform grants it. Do not delay reporting a genuine problem, because deadlines run from delivery, not from convenience. Do not use this design as legal advice about consumer rights in private sales, which vary by jurisdiction and by platform, and are governed by the applicable law and the platform's own terms. title: Signature Script Ear
body:
The Signature Script Ear is Manon's original design for hearing a fraud script by its markers rather than by its story, because advance-fee and fake-courier scripts charge for a delivery that never happens and then charge again for its release. The ear listens for payment before inspection, a fee to release a held parcel, a link from an unexpected message, pressure to act immediately, and refusal to meet or use the platform channel. One marker means stop and verify independently; two or more mean stop, keep the conversation as evidence, and report the account, because the markers together are the script and the script's purpose is visible in what it removes: the item, the inspection, and the protection.

Method. The working method for this record is script listening in the Signature style. First, the five script markers are stated. Second, each marker is marked present or absent in the conversation. Third, the verdict is read from the count. Fourth, a release fee from a message link is never paid; delivery is verified only through the platform or carrier's own site. Fifth, the demo listens to an example conversation showing one marker and prints the stop-and-verify verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature script ear. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: script markers found: 1; - fee to release held parcel; ear verdict: stop and verify independently Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand conversation, taught as a household rule, because these scripts target politeness, haste, and desire. Do not pay any fee to release a parcel not agreed in the platform's own messages. Do not follow delivery links from unexpected messages. Do not argue with a scripted account; stopping and reporting is the complete response. Do not use this design to accuse a legitimate seller whose genuine delivery problem looks similar; independent verification through the platform resolves the doubt. title: Signature Provenance Watch
body:
The Signature Provenance Watch is Manon's original design for refusing an item whose history the seller does not want examined, because buying a stolen item harms its true owner, risks confiscation without refund, and can draw the buyer into a police matter, all for a bargain that was never a bargain. The watch looks for an unexplained low price, removed or obscured marks, a vague or shifting origin story, pressure for speed and silence, and an unusual quantity of a commonly stolen type. One flag alone may be innocent, but several together describe an item whose provenance is being hidden, and the watch's answer at that point is to walk away rather than to bargain harder.

Method. The working method for this record is provenance watching in the Signature style. First, the five provenance flags are stated. Second, each flag is marked present or absent. Third, the verdict is read: zero or one flag means proceed with normal checks, two flags mean demand a clear origin account and documentary proof, and three or more mean walk away and consider reporting the listing. Fourth, if an item already bought proves stolen, the buyer seeks advice from the platform and the relevant authorities rather than reselling it. Fifth, the demo watches an example listing showing three flags and prints the walk-away verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature provenance watch. Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand purchase, and use it strictly for high-value, branded, and commonly stolen item types. Do not buy an item whose identifying marks have been deliberately removed, because removal has no innocent purpose in a sale. Do not use this design as legal advice about possession of stolen goods, which is governed by the applicable law and varies by jurisdiction. title: Signature Child-Safe Gate
body:
The Signature Child-Safe Gate is Manon's original design for children's secondhand items, and its rule is stricter than for any other goods: an unknown safety status is a refusal, not a question. The gate checks identifying details recorded, official recall listings checked, no recall found, safety parts complete, and safety inspection passed. A recall found closes the gate; an unchecked recall listing closes the gate; missing safety parts close the gate. The gate exists because a child's item can be recalled, damaged invisibly, or missing a safety part while still looking perfectly usable, and the cost of being wrong is paid by a child.

Method. The working method for this record is gate checking in the Signature style. First, the five gate conditions are stated. Second, each condition is marked met or not. Third, the verdict is read: all conditions met mean proceed with normal checks, any recall found or unknown status means do not buy. Fourth, the failing conditions are printed by name. Fifth, the demo runs the gate on an example item with a recall found and prints the do-not-buy verdict.

Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand children's item, including furniture, car seats, toys, and play equipment, without bargain exception. Do not buy a child's item with missing safety parts, broken mechanisms, or an unknown recall status. Do not rely on the seller's assurance about recalls; check the official listings yourself. title: Signature Grade Truth Table
body:
The Signature Grade Truth Table is Manon's original design for the three condition words sellers use as if they were one word: used, refurbished, and reconditioned. The table's rule is that the label is only a nickname and the written facts are the promise: what inspection was done, what parts were replaced or repaired, and what warranty applies and from whom. All three facts stated with a refurbisher warranty mean refurbished; wear disclosed without repair claims mean used; partial repair claims without a full warranty mean reconditioned or unclear. When label and facts disagree, the table trusts the facts, because the facts are what a dispute can hold.

Method. The working method for this record is truth-table classification in the Signature style. First, three example descriptions are stated with their grades. Second, each description is printed with its grade. Third, the rule is printed: trust the written facts, not the label alone. Fourth, the buyer prices the offer against the same grade elsewhere, not against a better grade. Fifth, the demo classifies the three examples and prints the rule.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature grade truth table. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. Use and limits. Use this design for every secondhand purchase where the condition word affects the price, and use it strictly for electronics and appliances where refurbishment claims are common. Do not pay a refurbished price for a used description, because the price gap is the value of the work and warranty claimed. Do not accept a refurbishment claim without the written facts behind it. title: Signature Secondhand Routine
body:
The Signature Secondhand Routine is Manon's original design for turning separate cautions into one habit that runs before, during, and after every purchase, because desire and urgency defeat memory and routines do not. The routine has three phases: before meeting, read the seller's history shape and agree safe ground; during the exchange, inspect with eyes first, prove the device, photograph the handover, and pay through the platform channel; after handover, check the item fully within the agreed window and keep the record. Written down and consulted before each purchase, the routine is a practice rather than a principle, and after any bad experience it is reviewed, because a routine that failed once contains the lesson for its own repair.

Method. The working method for this record is routine scoring in the Signature style. First, the routine's six steps are stated. Second, each step is marked followed or missed for a recent purchase. Third, the verdict is read: all six followed mean the routine held, four or five mean name the missed step and fix it next time, and fewer mean the routine is not yet a routine and must be written down and consulted first. Fourth, the missed steps are printed by name. Fifth, the demo scores an example purchase following three of six steps and prints the write-it-down verdict.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature secondhand routine. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: routine steps followed: 3 of 6; missed: ['safe ground agreed', 'handover album taken', 'record kept']; routine verdict: write the routine down and consult it first Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design as the household's secondhand rule, taught to everyone who buys or sells, because the routine protects the whole household's money and safety. Do not treat the routine as a guarantee, because no routine defeats every fraud, which is why platform payment and prompt reporting remain the backstops. Do not let the routine grow so long that it is skipped; six steps followed always beat twenty steps followed sometimes. Do not use this design as legal advice, because rights and remedies vary by platform and jurisdiction.
